---
title: "Welcome"
---

This handbook explains machine-learning concepts at four levels of depth. Each lesson begins with an accessible explanation and then progressively adds mechanism, mathematics, code, and modern systems context.

## The four levels

::: {.callout-note}
### Level 1 - Intuition

What is the concept, and why does it matter?
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Level 2 - Mechanics

How does it work step by step?
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Level 3 - Mathematics & Code

How can we express and implement it?
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Level 4 - Research & Systems

How does it behave in modern research and production systems?
:::

## How to use this book

You can read every level in sequence, or stop when the explanation reaches the depth you need. The code examples are intentionally small: their purpose is to make the underlying mechanism visible before introducing framework abstractions.

This prototype follows a dependency chain:

1. Gradient descent explains how parameters are updated.
2. Backpropagation explains how gradients are computed.
3. The artificial neuron provides the model whose parameters are trained.

## Prerequisites

No prior machine-learning experience is assumed. Basic algebra is useful, but the mathematical requirements are introduced as they become necessary.

## Prototype status

This is the initial prototype of the handbook. It is designed to test the lesson structure, level boundaries, code style, and Quarto presentation before the curriculum is expanded.
